codeFindings.detail: YES. catalog-crawler HTML branch calls adapter.getNextPageUrl($, currentUrl) (L494) and loops; buildPaginatedUrl for {type:'query',template:'page'} sets ?page=N (correct for this BC Stencil site). watermark-crawler navigate-from-watermark does the same (L644-649). getNextPageUrl (generic-retail.ts:1331-1355) reads '.pagination-item--next a' for BigCommerce. Live ?page=2 on equipment/ = 40 NEW cards, zero overlap with page 1 - HTML pagination works.

For non-WAF sites, products.length===0 breaks the INNER page loop (L484). The OUTER loop then advances urlIdx++ (L501-503), so a tile-only / empty parent yields 0 for THAT url and the walk continues to the next catalogUrl. The break is PER-URL, not catalog-fatal. So including low-yield parents like /firearms.html (31) or empty firearms leaves is not catastrophic - they just under-contribute. The real coverage limit here is structural (no all-products PLP; firearms/optics/ammo PLPs say 'There are no products').

Server: cloudflare + CF-RAY + __cf_bm on every response, but no-UA = 200 and zero challenge/cf-mitigated across the entire multi-hundred-request walk. Cloudflare passive. hasWaf=false correct; setting hasWaf=true would needlessly engage Playwright + drop perPage 50->20 (catalog-crawler.ts:290) with zero benefit.

case 'sitemap' builds `${origin}${m.url}`; an absolute m.url double-prefixes the origin and fetch fails -> null. validateMethod checks the method name only, not URL scheme. Today's R1 candidate's absolute productCountMethod.url would silently null the probe (only matters when expectedProductCount is absent, which it is not here - but the value is still wrong).

getCatalogUrls -> _getSiteSpecificUrls returns profile.catalogUrls (resolved to absolute against origin) when present, THEN appends generic fallbacks /categories.php, /shop/, /products, /. So DB/profile catalogUrls ARE consumed by the runtime; /categories.php is appended as an extra (it is a tile index = 0 cards, harmless per the per-URL break above).
